title: The Field Maker
summary: Find the field of a current element, a coil, an arc and two loops, with its direction.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 4.4, Magnetic field due to a current element, Biot-Savart law
concepts: Field at the centre of a coil
Field on the axis of a coil
learningOutcome: The student can find the size and direction of the field of a current element, a coil, an arc and concentric loops, and compare the field on the axis with the field at the centre.

levels.title: A current element
levels.adds: Baseline: dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl sin θ / r² with the direction from dl × r (Example 4.4).
hints: μ₀/4π = 10⁻⁷ T m/A. Change dl to metres.
Only the part of dl across the line to the point counts: sin θ.
The direction is that of dl × r: curl the fingers of the right hand from dl towards r.

levels.title: A coil
levels.adds: New idea: every turn of a tightly wound coil adds μ₀I/2R at the centre (Ex 4.1, Example 4.6).
hints: B = μ₀NI/2R at the centre. Change R to metres.
Each turn adds its own field in the same direction.
Curl the fingers along the current: the thumb gives the field.

levels.title: An arc
levels.adds: New idea: an arc gives the same fraction of the loop field as its angle, and straight leads in line with the centre give none (Example 4.5).
hints: For a straight lead in line with the centre dl × r = 0.
The arc gives its fraction of μ₀I/2R.
The direction follows the same right-hand rule as for a full loop.

levels.title: Along the axis
levels.adds: New idea: the field on the axis falls off from its value at the centre as R³/(R² + x²)^(3/2) (Section 4.5).
hints: B = μ₀NIR² / [2(R² + x²)^(3/2)]. Keep every length in metres.
At x = 0 it is the centre value μ₀NI/2R.
The fraction is the axis field divided by the centre field.

levels.title: Two loops
levels.adds: More steps: loops with a common centre add their fields if the currents go the same way and subtract if opposite.
hints: Find the field of each loop at the centre separately.
Same sense: add. Opposite senses: subtract.
The loop with the larger field decides the direction.

misconceptions: The field of a coil at its centre does not depend on the number of turns
A straight wire section in line with the point contributes the most
The field on the axis of a coil is the same everywhere along the axis
Currents in opposite senses in two loops add their fields
